EURC, Pyth, and the ERC-8004 Identity Registry mainnet addresses are still unpublished (docs.arc.io itself says mainnet addresses are not yet available) and confirmed by direct probe to have no code on chain 5042 — those integrations remain deferred. The RPC/explorer Arcodian points at for Arc Mainnet (arc-rpc.stakeme.pro / arc.exploreme.pro) is an unofficial third-party operator, not Circle's own. It was independently verified 2026-07-31 by cross-checking eth_chainId/net_version (5042), eth_getCode on both the native USDC precompile and our own already-deployed ArcPumpFactoryV8, and eth_getTransactionByHash/eth_getBalance for our own deployer address against what the explorer's own page independently rendered — all consistent. That verification does not make it Circle's own infrastructure. Swap it out (VITE_ARC_MAINNET_RPC / VITE_ARC_MAINNET_EXPLORER env overrides already exist in src/config.ts) the moment an official endpoint is public.

ArcBridgeRouter deployed 2026-07-31 to all 5 chains (Ethereum, Optimism, Arbitrum, Base, Arc) after arc-rpc.stakeme.pro proved Arc Mainnet was reachable. A prior deployment had a Solidity interface bug — declared depositForBurn as returning a uint64 nonce, but CCTP v2's real depositForBurn returns nothing, so the EVM's own ABI-decode reverted every burn on every chain since original deployment, undetected because the test suite's own mock made the identical wrong assumption. Root-caused via local anvil fork trace + Blockscout proxy-implementation ABI lookup, fixed, redeployed, and proven live: real transactions on all 5 chains including a full multi-hop round trip (Arc→Base, Arc→Arbitrum, claimed on both destinations), plus at least 3 independent third-party wallets (not ours) bridging on their own with no assistance, one of whom also independently claimed on the destination chain unaided. Sourcify+public-Blockscout source-verified on the 4 EVM chains; Arc's own third-party explorer's verify endpoint currently errors server-side on their end, unresolved.

Circle's own TokenMinter.burnLimitsPerMessage caps a single burn OUT of Arc Mainnet — a network-side rollout limit on Circle's side, not Arcodian's, that Circle raises over time without notice: 1 USDC when first confirmed 2026-07-31, already 100,000 USDC when re-checked live on-chain 2026-08-30. The frontend now reads this limit live (fetchBurnLimitPerMessage in bridgeRecovery.ts, 5-minute cache) instead of a hardcoded constant, so it tracks Circle's real ceiling automatically and surfaces a clear message (not a raw revert) if a burn exceeds it.

Official Arc Testnet Pyth deployment, 1% confidence guard, 20% deviation breaker are active. Freshness window changed 2026-07-27 from a hardcoded 1 hour to a per-market immutable maxOracleAge (90 hours for the live EUR/USD market) — the 1-hour bound was itself a bug: EUR/USD is a traditional-FX Pyth feed that only publishes during NY market hours and goes fully silent the whole weekend, so a 1-hour window falsely reverted OracleStale() every Friday close through Sunday reopen regardless of oracle health. The wider window is a deliberate tradeoff (weekend-safe vs. slower detection of a genuinely broken feed on a weekday) that an independent auditor should confirm explicitly, not inherit from this line.

50,000 USDC supply / 25,000 USDC borrow caps (raised 2026-07-27 from 100/50 USDC canary); live supply-collateral-borrow-repay-withdraw E2E completed with zero bad debt on the current ArcLendV2 deployment, with utilization/rate response verified against the exact curve formula.

Agent Pay factory has isolated immutable-owner vaults and no factory admin path into vault funds. ArcAgentPayV4 (2026-07-27) additionally requires the vault owner to still be an agentId's CURRENT Identity Registry owner at both setPolicy and payInvoice, closing a staleness gap where a resold agentId's stale passport binding could keep spending a previous owner's vault; live-confirmed against a real, externally-owned agentId. Prior V3 vaults are unaffected and keep working.

ArcAgentJobsV2 (redeployed 2026-07-27) now rejects job creation if the evaluator equals the client or the provider (SelfDealing()), closing a self-dealing hole where a client could unilaterally reject legitimate work or a provider could self-approve. Live-confirmed both the revert and that a normal 3-party job still succeeds.

ArcAdminTimelock (redeployed 2026-07-27) changed transferAdmin from a single unchecked step (no zero-address guard, a typo permanently bricked admin control) to a two-step propose/accept plus a separate explicit renounceAdmin. Live-proven both halves: a burn-address proposal left admin untouched and unacceptable by anyone, then a real propose->accept round-trip succeeded.

Unified monitoring and Pyth keeper timers are active and enabled. A 2026-07-27 systemd-wide sweep found 6 of these services (analytics/treasury/fx-stats/arcpay-stats/agentpay-index/monitor) had been silently failing on EVERY scheduled run since inception — each called an npm script that never existed in package.json — leaving their public data files frozen for roughly 2 days with zero error surfaced anywhere. All 6 fixed (pointed directly at their real scripts, matching the pattern the working indexers already used) and verified producing fresh output within seconds of the fix. A 7th bug (fx-stats.mjs had no checkpointing, so a full historical rescan could never finish inside its own timeout and looped forever) was fixed with the same incremental-checkpoint pattern arcpay-stats.mjs already used.
Mainnet deployment remains disabled unless every explicit release variable and sign-off is supplied.

Governance on every one of these is deployer-only (no mainnet multisig deployed yet) — see the admin-handoff-safety and role-separation gates above, which describe the mechanism, not that it has actually been handed off on mainnet. V8's factory has since been superseded for new launches: marketUsdcFactoryV9 (0x6e1d1a09...195f9, redeployed 2026-08-02 for a treasury-wiring bug) then marketUsdcFactoryV10 (0xCEc317Ca...19cED) graduate into real permissionless Uniswap V3 pools instead of ArcPairFactoryV2 — see the graduation-pool-griefing gate below for an open risk specific to that V9/V10 graduation path. Full address list and rationale: public/developers/contracts.mainnet.json and contracts/DEPLOYMENT.md's 'Arc Mainnet — Phase 1' section.

Found in a 2026-08-30 self-review of ArcPumpV9/ArcPumpV10 (the two contracts actually receiving new mainnet launches): both pre-created each launch's Uniswap V3 pool at launch time via v3Factory.createPool(), deliberately left uninitialized so bots could see the pair early. UniswapV3Pool.initialize() has no access control, so anyone could call it first and set an arbitrary sqrtPriceX96 before graduation; _graduate() only initialized if existingPrice == 0, and its positionManager.mint() call used amount0Min: 0 / amount1Min: 0, so a front-run price was accepted silently — most of that launch's intended liquidity could end up unused and permanently stranded (no rescue function, buy/sell blocked once graduated=true). FIXED and REDEPLOYED to Arc Mainnet 2026-08-30: ArcPumpFactoryV10 0xCf93231d55dA8Df1300619615b453e4EeAB6feD3 (was 0xCEc317Ca96b7e55FA0F9f7C243cDb0ee6BC19cED, now marketUsdcFactoryV10LegacyPoolGriefing in contracts.mainnet.json) — createLaunch() no longer pre-creates the pool; _graduate() now creates+initializes it atomically in the same transaction, closing the window entirely, and a defense-in-depth branch (POOL_PRICE_MANIPULATED) reverts graduation if a pool is somehow already initialized at a price more than MINT_SLIPPAGE_BPS (2%) off the curve's own fair price, with a real amount0Min/amount1Min floor on the mint instead of 0. Same v3Factory/positionManager/treasury/graduationThreshold (12,000 ether) as the old factory — verified against the new deployment's own constructor-state getters, not just the deploy script's log. Covered by contracts/test/ArcPumpV10Graduation.t.sol (4 tests: no pre-create, normal graduation, manipulated-price revert, fair-pre-existing-pool success) — full forge test suite 318/318 passing. src/config.ts ARC_MAINNET_CONTRACTS.marketUsdcFactoryV10 and scripts/mainnet-market-index.mjs's FACTORIES both re-pointed; frontend build/deploy pending as a separate step. ArcPumpV9 is unchanged (legacy, existing launches only, no new launches route through it) and still carries this issue; not fixed since patching it would require redeploying a factory whose only live launch ('Architects') cannot be migrated. The old V10 factory's existing launches are likewise not migratable and stay indexed/tradeable there under the legacy address.
